newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kerry Securities to scale down operation - report.
newsitem.headline: Kerry Securities to scale down operation - report.

text.p: Kerry Securities will scale down operations, cutting about 40 local staff and shutting down overseas offices, Hong Kong newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Kerry Securities officials were not immediately available to comment. Kerry Securities planned to close its institutional investment services unit in Hong Kong and switch its focus to private investors, the newspaper reports said.

It would shut the local research department and sack more staff later after reviewing the restructuring, the reports in the South China Morning Post, Hong Kong Economic Journal and Hong Kong Economic Times said.
Kerry Securities is a brokerage firm equally owned by Malaysian businessman Robert Kuok, who controls the Kuok Group, and the firm's former joint managing director Jeremy King.
The brokerage is also considering closing overseas offices including a subsidary in London, and examining the viability of its research division in New York, the reports said.
Kerry Securities would continue to act as a broker, retaining its membership in the Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, they said.
